answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by requiring each agent to post a unique stake of saffron-derived collateral that represents scarce physical resources. When suspicious activity emerges from the ocean of potential fake identities, the protocol examines the nadir of the attacker’s total committed value; if it falls below a threshold, all associated stakes are slashed, making large-scale identity farming economically irrational and protecting the network’s integrity.
